## Gates — every exit code captured to a file BEFORE any pipe

Run twice, from the worktree, each as
`node scripts/X.mjs > file 2>&1; EXIT=$?; echo "$EXIT" > file.exit` — first on `eae77bd91`,
then **re-run on `ed2ab5078`**, the head after `origin/main` (`bbba09840`) was merged in.
Both runs are 0 across the board; the verdict lines below are from the second.

| gate | exit | its own printed verdict line |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check-changeset-presence` | 0 | "No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed." — 2 files changed, 0 published source, 0 manifests |
| `check-changeset-overwrite` | 0 | report-only. Both entries listed with `declared at base` **equal to** `declares now` — its documented **case 2**, a prose correction with every declared package name kept |
| `check-changeset-claims` | 0 | "No pending changeset names a file this change touches." — 0 files changed outside `.changeset/`, 1636 pending in total |
| `check-pending-changeset-literals` | 0 | "No test source names a pending changeset." |
| `check-changeset-no-major` | 0 | "No changeset declares a `major` bump." |
| `check-changeset-fixed` | 0 | "All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group." |
| `check-control-bytes` | 0 | "OK (scanned 7822 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)." |
| `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` | 0 | "VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only" |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` (both paths) | 0 | "NOT GOVERNED — 2 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched." |

Beyond the nine gates, a second control-byte scan was run directly over the two edited
files for the non-NUL control range as well: zero hits, and the scan's own exit code was
captured before any pipe.

⚠️ **Declared narrowing.** No package source moved, so there is no affected-package build
closure and no package `test` / `typecheck` owed. The repository-level scans that
`.changeset/**` triggers — `Lint`, `Type Check`, the four `Test` shards, `Build & E2E`,
`Build Docs` — are CI's runs, not this seat's, and are left to converge on this PR. That
narrowing is declared rather than silent.

## ② The BORN FALSE half — verified AT THE WRITE-TIME REF, which is the only place it can be

This is the claim that matters, because ⭐ **born-false can only be established at the ref where the sentence was written** — measuring today proves nothing about it. Read at `adf581278`, the commit that wrote the `8802-…` entry:

```
:21  titleField: z.string().optional().describe('Title field'),
:25  allowCollapse: z.boolean().optional().describe('Allow columns to collapse/expand'),
```

⇒ on the **day that entry was written**, the surviving `ObjectKanbanSchema` face **declared both keys** — while the entry said 「The surviving `ObjectKanbanSchema` face declares none of them」. **BORN FALSE, confirmed at its own ref.**

⭐ And the PR gets the subtlety right, which is easy to miss: those two keys are named in the sentence's *refused-by-name* clause, and that clause **is** true of the surviving face — it does not refuse them. What was false is 「declares none of them」. One sentence, one clause true and one false, and the repair says so instead of averaging them.

## ③ The ROTTED half, and every row of both tables checked against an enumerated list

⛔ Not spot-checked per key. The declared property list of `ObjectKanbanSchema` on `origin/main` was enumerated in full:

`allowCollapse cardFields cardTitle columns conditionalFormatting coverImageField filter groupBy groupField limit objectName onCardClick onCardMove onQuickAdd quickAdd titleField type`

Against it, **every row of both tables holds**: `columns` and `cardTitle` declared (ROTTED, falsified by objectui#8913 and objectui#9606); `titleField` and `allowCollapse` declared (BORN FALSE); `filter` declared (ROTTED, objectui#8174); and `swimlaneField`, `grouping`, `navigation`, `cardTemplates`, `columnWidths`, `draggable`, `onColumnAdd`, `onCardAdd` **absent from the list**, exactly as the table says.

⚠️ One control of mine was ambiguous and was resolved rather than reported: a grep for `swimlaneField|onCardAdd` inside the schema block returned **1**, which looks like a declaration and is not — it is a mention inside the `allowCollapse` refusal message's prose (`:86`). ⭐ A key-shaped token inside a **string** is not a declaration; enumerating property lines is the instrument that can tell them apart, and a substring grep is not.

## ④ ⭐ The deepest thing in this PR, and it is not in the card

The `7322-…` repair does not stop at re-dating five rotted readings. It states, and then **obeys**, the rule that follows:

> 「⛔ Every reading below therefore carries the date it was taken, and none is restated in the undated present tense — that tense is the construction that rotted, and a re-measurement written in it would only rot again **before this entry publishes**.」

⇒ the implementer declined to re-measure into the present tense at all. ⭐ That is the general lesson the card was groping for and did not have: for a file that publishes **verbatim at an unknown future date**, a fresh measurement written in the present tense is not a fix — it is the same defect with a newer number. The only durable repair is a **dated** reading, or no figure.

It also found **five** rotted readings in `7322-…` that the card never named, each with its falsifying card and landing date.
